spoken: [hook] You don't have a motivation problem. You have a size problem. || When a goal is too big, your brain can't see where to start. So it does the easiest thing, it waits for tomorrow. || Take writing a book. That's three hundred pages. Nobody can start three hundred pages on a Tuesday night. || [turn] So shrink it until the first step is obvious. Outline the first chapter this week. Then write three hundred words a day. || Same with getting fit. Don't start with a six day gym program. Walk thirty minutes after dinner, three days this week. || Here's a simple test. If you can't start the first step in under fifteen minutes, it's still too big. Break it down again. || [land] Every small step you finish gives you a little proof that you can do it. And that proof is what motivation actually feels like. || [outro] That's what Dmyor is for. You archive your dream today, so you can see it tomorrow, and break it down into small steps you can actually do. || [outro] If you want to try it out, I've put the link in the bio.
